primitives.name: Seasonal Linear Predictivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Here we show that, despite the large number of confounding factors, the results of a football team in longer competitions (e.g., a national league) follow a basically linear trend useful for predictive purposes, too.
primitives.assumptions: The underlying dynamics of team performance in a long-term league follow a linear trajectory, independent of short-term fluctuations and external noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Nonlinear regime occurs when sudden rule changes, catastrophic injuries, or extreme managerial interventions disrupt the established linear progression.

layer2.mapping: GSI: The linear trend represents the posterior mean of a Gaussian process prior; GSE: The linear fit serves as a baseline state-transition kernel for situational reasoning.
layer2.telemetry: Residual variance of accumulated points after linear detrending, monitored for anomaly detection.

primitives.name: Simple Linear Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: Here we restrict to national football (soccer) championships and the simplest possible (predictive) statistical techinque, i.e., linear regression as in [36,37].
primitives.assumptions: The relationship between match rounds and accumulated points is approximated by a straight line, minimizing squared error loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violates when heteroscedasticity or autocorrelation in residuals indicates omitted variable bias or non-stationarity.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Linear regression maps historical data to a predictive posterior distribution via conjugate priors; GSE: It defines a deterministic transition kernel for state evolution under constant drift.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error on holdout validation sets, cross-validated across different training window lengths.

primitives.name: Accumulated Points Time Series
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper we want to demonstrate that, despite the existing randomness and other confounding factors, there are situations where the sport results are driven by very simple (for instance, linear) trends, and these trends can be captured by basic techniques and limited amount of training data.
primitives.assumptions: Points accumulate deterministically plus independent identically distributed noise, forming a discrete-time signal with additive structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the time series exhibits structural breaks, regime shifts, or becomes non-stationary due to external shocks.

layer2.mapping: GSI: The time series is modeled as a latent Gaussian process; GSE: It encodes the state-transition function for cumulative score evolution in sequential decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Autocorrelation function decay rate, indicating persistence versus mean-reversion behavior.

Anti-collinearity is enforced by selecting independent covariates (rounds vs. points), preventing leakage between training and test sets.
